suggestions.title: 1. MDMA: what "too late for an easy fix" means, and sodium and magnesium in the seizure line
suggestions.what: Two places in your MDMA paragraph. "(sodium might be too low and it could be too late for an easy fix)" becomes "(sodium might be too low by then for an electrolyte drink to fix; while you wait for medics, if they're alert and not vomiting, give them something very salty instead, like strong broth or salty snacks)". "A seizure or collapse can result from low potassium," becomes "A seizure or collapse can result from low sodium, magnesium or potassium,". Nothing else changes.
suggestions.tested: Your version read [Human High 132](https://www.pangram.com/history/c45651d9-f45e-4f3e-8496-f340eae874b0); with both fixes as here, after your message of 15:41 UTC (salty food while waiting; magnesium), [Human Written, 0% AI, one window Human High](https://www.pangram.com/history/597c5351-fd56-4dbf-9b27-038b9c2d4de5) over all 157 words. The first wording, "so don't give them any more to drink", read [Human High 142](https://www.pangram.com/history/e1cf44d8-f5fe-4a33-98ac-24780393acd7).
suggestions.why: Your questions: no more electrolyte drinks once those signs show, since they carry far less salt than blood and still thin it (the wilderness-medicine guidelines name water and sports drinks as the cause of low sodium from overdrinking, and restrict fluids once it's suspected); and yes to something hypertonic: the same guidelines treat mild low sodium with salt by mouth, a very strong broth or salty food, when the person is alert and can keep it down, and MDMA harm-reduction advice says the same (salty snacks, less water, get ready to get help). Hospitals use a concentrated salt drip. "Too late for an easy fix" read as "nothing can be done", and a fresh reader of my first wording couldn't tell whether to call or to feed them, so it now says "while you wait for medics". And the seizure line: low sodium and low magnesium both bring seizures, and low magnesium often brings low potassium with it and keeps potassium from coming back up, which fits your magnesium-first experience; very low potassium brings weakness and heart rhythm trouble.
suggestions.stays: Every other word of your paragraph, and your sipping line before the signs, which is for before any of them show.
suggestions.deciding: Approve puts both in. Revise if you'd say them your way. The fresh readers also asked two things, not changed: the seizure line names causes but no action (your "The following indicators would justify calling medics:" covers it), and "like my second wife had" is your story from the paragraph before.
suggestions.advice_note: Approve: both hold up against the sources, and the paragraph still reads Human High.

edits.before: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low and it could be too late for an easy fix). If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.
edits.after: Once their jaw tenses, that should be their last dose of MDMA, so get them to slow down and cool off. If they drink a lot of plain water, even a single normal MDMA dose raises the risk of their sodium dropping too low, so have them sip an electrolyte drink when they're thirsty instead. The following indicators would justify calling medics: If their confusion or headache worsens, or vomiting won't stop (sodium might be too low by then for an electrolyte drink to fix; while you wait for medics, if they're alert and not vomiting, give them something very salty instead, like strong broth or salty snacks). If their muscles keep getting weaker or their heart palpitations keep getting stronger, that could be from dangerously low potassium, like my second wife had. A seizure or collapse can result from low sodium, magnesium or potassium, and can also come from overheating or MDMA toxicity.
